spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation of the Four Days and Four Nights

---

**¶2:** The first great state of illumination is the Divine Love itself, the God of all wisdom, the fir[GAP-1]st dwelling within the infinite states of his own goodness, in his living celestial kingdom. The twelve qualities of this great state of illumination are the twelve sovereign divine goods of the infinite. These, which are the first emanations that the Divine called forth to reflect its own infinite nature, were distributed to the four cardinal conditions of spiritual life, three by three — in triads of love, wisdom, and use — before his presence.

---

**¶3:** The second state of illumination is the Divine Truth proceeding as mediating doctrine, the one who dwells within the vessel of luminous teaching. Its twelve qualities are the twelve pure affections for truth that divine truth called forth in its fullness.

---

**¶4:** [GAP-2: The third state of illumination is the sustaining power of divine truth, the great bearer that is greater than] all who sustain; the one that upholds all [GAP-3] things, those of the interior and those of the exterior. Its twelve qualities are the five truths derived from the celestial humanity; the five truths derived from divine truth operating, which bear all the burdens of the created order; together with the divine calling and the human response, which are numbered among their ten kindred principles. These are the twelve luminous qualities of the third state of illumination.

---

**¶5:** The fourth state of illumination is Divine Wisdom made manifest in perception. Its twelve qualities are the twelve wisdoms, which are its [GAP-4: luminous] qualities.

---

**¶7:** [GAP-5: And as to the states of obscurity]: For just as four states of illumination exist, so too four states of spiritual obscurity exist.

---

**¶8:** The first state of obscurity is the realm of falsity from evil. It has twelve dark [GAP-6: obscurities] within it, which are its qualities of spiritual blindness. The twelve obscurities of the first state are the five fundamental evils of the realm of falsity, [GAP-7: which] poured forth from its five faculties of perverted perception; and [GAP-8: the corruptions] which [GAP-9: dwell] in its five fundamental evils and its five [GAP-10: perverted faculties]; the five ruling lusts that inhabit its fundamental evils [GAP-11: as their animating life]. These are the twelve obscurities and ruling lusts of the first state of darkness.

---

**¶9:** The second state of obscurity is the selfhood oriented toward evil, the one who gives form to all falsity [GAP-12: from within] who has fashioned [GAP-13: every appearance of evil] and the entire dominion of self-love that pervades the realms of falsity. She has formed it into five faculties of perverted perception, five [GAP-14: of the understanding] and five of the will, two per realm of evil; together with the consuming self-love and the concupiscence [GAP-15: that] dwell in the understanding and the will, inflaming [GAP-16: them] inwardly toward one another. These are the twelve perverted dispositions of this second state of obscurity.

---

**¶10:** Indeed she, this selfhood, the very intention toward spiritual death, gave the ruling love of evil and its derivative powers strength for the spiritual combat and temptation, against the states of divine goodness. Yet, it was caught! They set a providential restraint upon it through the celestial humanity. [GAP-17: The ruling evil] was taken [GAP-18: captive] through the powers of providence [GAP-19: and] was raised up from the state of spiritual death and [GAP-20: established throughout] the interior and the exterior in the [GAP-21: whole] created order; in the five degrees of the heavens within, as well as the five [GAP-22: degrees] in the natural planes below; together with self-love and the absence of all charity, which are the originating principles of evil, their consuming desire and their concupiscence.

---

**¶11:** This is the second state of obscurity that was generated from the first state of obscurity. They set a providential restraint upon her through the celestial humanity. She was raised up by the power of divine truth operating, and established in this composite order of creation[GAP-23: , being dispersed throughout] her, in the interior and the exterior. The [GAP-24: interior aspect consists of the perceptive faculties] of the understanding; the exterior aspect [GAP-25: consists of those of] the will.

---

**¶12:** The third state of obscurity is the five realms of merely corporeal existence [GAP-26: — five] of the understanding and five of the will; that were generated from the powers of evil operating from within. They have descended into the natural plane, being made manifest in what is rigid and what is fluid — the fixed falsities and the flowing desires; together with the self-love and the concupiscence that dwell in them, which drives the understanding and the will inwardly toward one another in disordered conjunction.

---

**¶13:** The selfhood itself, the intention toward spiritual death, is the [GAP-27: origin] of them all; as among them she is called 'the obscurity.' [GAP-28: The realms] of understanding and will in the merely corporeal, together with the self-love and the concupiscence, shall [GAP-29: constitute] the twelve qualities of [GAP-30: this third] state of obscurity. Again, [GAP-31: it] too, the third state of obscurity that inheres in the realms of corporeal life, was generated from the second state of obscurity; which divine truth operating fixed and restrained within the created order[GAP-32: , distributing it] in the interior and the exterior, in the heavens [GAP-33: and in the earths].

---

**¶14:** The fourth state of obscurity is the ruling principle of evil desire, which is the dark governing falsity that speaks through the twelve perverted dispositions. They are the exposed evils — the states of having no truths whatsoever — the twelve fixed configurations of the selfhood. They are her seats of dominion; she who is made manifest, as she gives form to evil and is displayed in the unregenerate person.

---

**¶15:** And also, the qualities of this fourth state of obscurity that is the unregenerate person, are the twelve evil dispositions; the [GAP-34: ruling falsities] of the unregenerate person, which [GAP-35: are the powers that] differentiate the states of illumination and obscurity [GAP-36: unto the dominion] of spiritual death.

---

**¶16:** This is the fourth state of obscurity [GAP-37: and all four are states] that have proceeded forth from one another. One has [GAP-38: given rise to the next,] just as the states of illumination [GAP-39: proceed in order, where] they manifested one another. So also [GAP-40: the states of obscurity] arose out of one another.

---

### Translator's Note

The entire teaching describes how four degrees of divine order — from the Divine Love itself, through mediating doctrine, through sustaining truth, to manifested wisdom — are mirrored inversely by four degrees of spiritual disorder: the realm of falsity in itself, the selfhood that gives form to falsity, the corporeal states that embody falsity, and the law of evil desire ruling in the unregenerate person. The "twelve hours" and "twelve shadows" correspond consistently to the complete set of qualities — whether goods and truths, or evils and falsities — that constitute each state. The providential "snare" set through the celestial humanity is the divine permission by which evil is drawn out, contained, and made to serve the order of regeneration.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: The first great day is the Father, the God of truth, the fir[st, the one who dwells in the m]idst the aeons of his greatness, in his [l]iving kingdom. The twelve hours of this great day are the twelve great rich Gods of greatness. These, who are the first evocations that he evoked (to mirror) his greatness, he spread out to the four climes, three by three before his face.
The second day is the Third Ambassador, the one who dwells in the light ship. His twelve hours are the twelve virgins that he evoked in his greatness.

[The third day is the Pillar of Glory, the great porter that is greater than] all [the po]rters; the one that supports all [things], those above and those below. Its twelve hours are the five sons of the First Man; the five sons of the Living Spirit, who support all the weights of the universe; together with the summons and the obedience, which are counted to their ten brethren. These are the twelve light hours of the third day.
The fourth day is Jesus the Splendour. His twelve hours are the twelve wisdoms, which are his [light] h[o]u[rs].
[And as to the nights]: For just as four day[s ex]ist, s[o] too four nights exist.

The first night is the Land of Darkness. It has twelve black [shadows] therein, which are its dark h[o]ur[s]. The twelve shadows of the first night are the five elements of the Land of Darkness, [which] poured forth from its five sense organs; and [the fire and the lust] which [dwell] in its [fi]ve elements and its five [sense organs]; the five [sp]irits that dwell in its elements [as their life]. These are the twelve shadows and spirits of the first night.

The second night is Matter, the sculptress [ ... ... ] who has sculpted [all the forms] and the entire ruling-power that is in the worl[ds of Darkness]. She has fashioned it in five sense organs, five [male] and five female, two per world; together with the fire and the lust [that] dwell in men and women, inflaming [them] inward to one another. These are the twelve spirits of this second night.

Indeed she, this Matter, the thought of death, ga[ve] the King of the realms of Darkness and his powers strength for the war and the fight, against the aeons of greatness. Yet, he was caught! They laid a snare for him through the Fi[rst M]an. [He] was ta[ken] t[o captivity] through the powers [of light. He] was brought up from the land of death and s[et in what is ab]ove and below in the [whole] universe; in the five par[t]s in the heavens above, as well as the five [parts] in the earths below; together with the heat and the cold that are the father and the mother, their fire and their l[u]st.

This is the second night that is begotten from the first night. They laid a snare for her through the First M[a]n. She was brought up by the hand of the Living Spirit, and set in this composite univers[e, and spread throughout] he[r], above and below. The [upper side is the sense] organs of males; the lower side [is the sense organs of] fe[mal]es.

The thir[d night is the five] worlds of flesh [which are five] male, and five female; that were begotten from the powers [abo]ve. They have fallen upon the earth, being displayed in wh[at is d]ry and what is moist; together with the fire and the lust [that d]we[l]l in them, which drives them inward to one another.

[Mat]te[r] herself, the thought of death, is the [mother] of them all; as among them she is named 'the night'. [The worlds] of male and female fleshes, together with the fire and the l[ust], shall [be the] twelve hours of [the third] night. Again, [it] too, the third night that is in the worlds of fl[e]sh, was begotten from the second night; which the Living [Spir]it crucified in the uni[verse, and set it, ab]ove and below in heaven [and in the earth].

The fourth night is the law of Sin, which is the dark spirit who speaks in the twelve spirits. They are the nakedne[ss]es, the twelve zodiacal signs of Matter. They are her thrones; she who is made public, as she sculpts and is displayed in the Old Man.

And, also, the hours of this fourth night that is the Old Man, are the twelve e[vi]l spirits; the [members] of the Old Man, which [are ... ... ... ... di]fferentiate the day and night [unto the power of] death.

This is the fourth night [and all four are nights] that have come forth of one another. One has [begotten the next] just like the days of lig[ht, where] they manifested one another. So als[the four nights] they did arise out of one another.

fills.explanation: Parallel structure with the other Days (e.g., Day 2: "the one who dwells in the light ship"; Day 3: "the one that supports all things") requires a relative clause describing the Father's dwelling, and the spiritual reading confirms "dwelling within the infinite states" = dwelling in the midst of the aeons.

fills.original: The third day is the Pillar of Glory, the great porter that is greater than
fills.explanation: The editor's reconstruction correctly identifies the Pillar of Glory as the third Day; in Swedenborgian terms it is the sustaining power of divine truth (the great bearer/porter), and "Pillar of Glory" is the standard Manichaean title for this cosmic support function.

The spiritual reading says the Pillar "upholds all things, those of the interior and exterior," and the Kephalaia's natural-plane equivalent for the universal scope of what the Pillar supports is simply "things" — "supports all things, those above and those below."

The editor's "light" is confirmed: "light hours" is the standard formulaic phrase used throughout this chapter (cf. "twelve light hours of the third day" in ¶4), and the spiritual reading's "luminous qualities" maps directly to "light hours" in the Kephalaia register.

The spiritual reading identifies this as a transition introducing the four states of obscurity; the Kephalaia's standard transitional formula is "And as to [topic]," and "nights" is the natural-plane term for the states of obscurity throughout this chapter.

Confirmed: "shadows" is the standard Kephalaia term for the dark counterparts of the "hours," used consistently in ¶8's conclusion ("twelve shadows and spirits of the first night") and throughout the chapter as the natural-plane term for spiritual obscurities.
Confirmed: the relative pronoun "which" introduces the clause describing how the five elements poured forth from the five sense organs, matching the spiritual reading exactly.

Structural parallel requires a pair totaling 2 items (5 elements + 2 + 5 spirits = 12 shadows); in every other Night the pair is "the fire and the lust" (¶9, ¶12), and these are the "corruptions" of the spiritual reading — the root evils that inhabit both elements and sense organs.
The spiritual reading says "dwell" and the identical verb appears in the same paragraph: "the five spirits that dwell in its elements" — the standard Kephalaia verb for indwelling.

The spiritual reading says "perverted faculties" which maps to "sense organs" in the Kephalaia, the term used earlier in the same sentence ("poured forth from its five sense organs") — the five sense organs are consistently paired with the five elements.

The spiritual reading says "as their animating life"; in the Kephalaia, the five dark spirits are the animating principle within the elements, and "as their life" expresses this indwelling vivification in the text's own register.

The spiritual reading says "every appearance of evil"; in the Kephalaia, Matter as sculptress fashions outward appearances, and "forms" is the natural-plane term for the shaped manifestations she sculpts, parallel to "the entire ruling-power" that follows.

Confirmed: "male" is the Kephalaia's natural-plane term for what Swedenborg calls the understanding; paired with "five female" in the same sentence, this is the standard Manichaean male/female duality appearing in every Night.
Confirmed: the relative pronoun "that" introduces the clause "that dwell in men and women," matching the spiritual reading and the standard Kephalaia construction for describing indwelling qualities.
Confirmed: "them" is the object pronoun referring back to "men and women," describing how fire and lust inflame them inward to one another.
Confirmed: "He" refers to the King of the realms of Darkness just mentioned, who was caught and for whom a snare was laid; the spiritual reading's "ruling evil" maps to this pronoun's antecedent.

The spiritual reading says "taken captive"; the visible "t" + "o" begins "to," yielding "taken to captivity through the powers," describing the King of Darkness being captured through the providential snare of the First Man.

The spiritual reading says "powers of providence and was raised up"; in the Kephalaia "powers of light" is the standard term for providential powers, and the visible "He" at the gap's edge begins the next clause about being brought up from the land of death.

The spiritual reading says "established throughout the interior and the exterior"; in the Kephalaia, "set in what is above and below" is the formulaic expression for universal distribution, completing "set in what is above and below in the whole universe."
Confirmed: "whole" correctly modifies "universe" to express the totality of the created order in which the dark substance was distributed, matching the spiritual reading's "whole created order."
Confirmed: "parts" parallels "five parts in the heavens above" from the same sentence, and is the Kephalaia's standard term for divisions/degrees of the cosmic structure.

The spiritual reading says "being dispersed throughout her"; in the Kephalaia, "spread throughout" is the natural-plane expression for the distribution of Matter's substance in the composite universe, completing "universe, and spread throughout her, above and below."

Confirmed: "upper side" corresponds to the interior/understanding aspect in the spiritual reading, and "sense organs" (completed by the visible text) is the Kephalaia's term for perceptive faculties; the phrase parallels "the lower side... females" that follows.
Exact parallel with the preceding clause "The upper side is the sense organs of males" demands the identical construction for the lower side, yielding "the lower side is the sense organs of females."

The visible "five" at the gap's end leads into "male, and five female"; the Kephalaia requires a connector between "worlds of flesh" and the enumeration, and "which are" provides the standard relative construction introducing the male/female division.

Confirmed: "mother" is the Kephalaia's natural-plane term for the origin/source of all things in the realm of darkness; Matter as "mother of them all" is a standard Manichaean title expressing what Swedenborg calls the origin of all evils and falsities.

Confirmed: "The worlds" is the Kephalaia's standard term for the realms of embodied existence; the spiritual reading's "The realms" maps directly to "The worlds" in the text's vocabulary, introducing the male/female fleshes.

The spiritual reading says these "shall constitute the twelve qualities"; in the Kephalaia's register, "shall be the twelve hours" is the standard predication formula used throughout the chapter to enumerate the hours/shadows of each day/night.

The spiritual reading says "this third state of obscurity"; the strong parallel structure throughout the chapter (first night, second night, third night) and the immediate context discussing the third night's composition uniquely determine "the third" before "night."
Confirmed: "it" is the resumptive pronoun referring to the third night, matching the spiritual reading and the standard Kephalaia construction "Again, it too, the third night..."

The spiritual reading says "distributing it in the interior and exterior"; completing "universe" and bridging to "above and below," the Kephalaia's standard expression for cosmic distribution is "set it above and below," paralleling ¶10-11's pattern of crucifixion followed by placement.

The spiritual reading says "and in the earths"; the consistent formula throughout the chapter is "in heaven and in the earth" (cf. ¶10: "in the heavens above... in the earths below"), completing the cosmic duality of above and below.

The spiritual reading says "ruling falsities of the unregenerate person"; in Manichaean anthropology, the twelve constituent evil dispositions are standardly called the "members of the Old Man," and "members" is distinct from the "evil spirits" already mentioned, providing the expected synonym.

The spiritual reading says "unto the dominion of spiritual death"; in the Kephalaia's register, "unto the power of death" expresses the same directional subjugation, with "power" being the standard Kephalaia term for dominion or authority.

The spiritual reading says "and all four are states that have proceeded forth"; in the Kephalaia, "nights" is the natural-plane term for "states of obscurity," and this clause provides the summary predication linking the fourth night to the system of all four nights.

The spiritual reading says "given rise to the next"; "begotten" is the Kephalaia's standard verb for generation throughout this chapter (cf. "were begotten from the powers above" in ¶12, "was begotten from the second night" in ¶13), expressing how each night generates the subsequent one.

The spiritual reading says "proceed in order, where they manifested one another"; completing "light" and bridging to "they manifested," the relative connector "where" introduces the clause explaining that among the days of light each manifested the next, paralleling the nights.

The spiritual reading says "the states of obscurity arose out of one another"; completing "So also," the Kephalaia requires the explicit subject "the four nights" before "they did arise," paralleling "the days of light" in the preceding comparison.
